objective: Finish four already-installed M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in a representative ODRI actuator shell-base fixture. Hold a straight tang break-off mandrel coaxially in each recessed insert, strike it with a separately manipulated hammer to fracture the modeled notched tang, withdraw it without displacing the retained insert, and physically recover all four free tangs into the tray. Full success requires four credited contact-caused fractures, four retained undamaged inserts, four distinct fragments resting in the tray, released tools, a valid RGB-D camera, and a stable two-second terminal state.
instruction: Break the tang from each of the four installed thread inserts using the straight mandrel and hammer. Keep every insert and the shell undamaged. Find each released tang, place all four in the collection tray, and release both tools.
industrial_mapping: The pinned Open Dynamic Robot Initiative actuator-module-v1 shell-preparation instructions specify four M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in the shell base, removal of their tangs with a tang break-off tool, and verification that tangs do not remain inside the part (source s-df759bd2377bbb57, pinned commit 66af1522b4fba0ec4a1d7790e66f5e4652208d30). The Böllhoff HELICOIL Plus manufacturer catalog states that the tang is broken at its notch, depicts hammer actuation of a straight mandrel on page 17, and lists straight mandrel 0158 040 1000 for M2.5 on page 55 (source s-6195df1bebbb33ef). The fixture is an independently authored representative rigid test article, not an exact current ODRI product or a scale reconstruction of the historical unitless STL.
damage_rules: Native joint breakage and component displacement must never be suppressed because a strike is invalid. Log every native attached-to-free transition separately from credited-valid-fracture events; invalid physical breakage remains visible and causes hard failure.

At reset, clear contact-pair episode IDs, impulse accumulators, native-transition records, credit records, hold timers, and camera freshness counters before the first physics step. At each POST_PHYSICS_STEP callback, consume only contacts stamped for the just-completed native step. Integrate contact impulse using the callback dt and the runtime-reported contact force in newtons; reject missing, stale, duplicated, non-finite, or unit-unverified readings.

A continuous strike begins on hammer-head–mandrel contact onset and ends only after that pair separates for at least one completed physics step. Adjacent solver samples during uninterrupted contact share one episode ID and cannot be counted as additional hammer blows.

For a strike episode, axial impulse is the sum over fresh hammer-head–mandrel samples of max(0, force dot the target insert axis) multiplied by callback dt. Off-axis impulse is the norm of the time-integrated force component perpendicular to that axis across all fresh contacts involving the mandrel, target insert, tang, or boss during the episode.

Shell contact-damage work is the cumulative positive closing contact work over shell/boss contacts: sum max(0, force dot negative relative contact-point velocity) multiplied by callback dt. The accumulator is monotonic from reset. Shell work above 0.02 J, visible shell fracture, or hammer-head–shell contact is irreversible hard failure.

Post-fracture forbidden penetration is the maximum positive signed overlap of the mandrel beyond the target tang-notch plane along the insert axis into the authored retained-coil or shell forbidden volumes, computed from collision geometry after the native fracture. More than 0.2 mm is irreversible hard failure.
Insert translation above 0.25 mm from its authored seat, rotation above 3 degrees from its authored orientation, coil-proxy fracture, or unthreading is irreversible hard failure.

A native tang fracture earns credit only when its single continuous hammer-head–mandrel episode supplies 0.012–0.035 N*s axial impulse, no more than 0.008 N*s off-axis impulse, no more than 5 degrees axis error, and no more than 0.35 mm radial offset. A fracture caused by another force path remains native breakage but is uncredited hard failure.

More than three distinct hammer-head–mandrel contact episodes for one insert, any strike after that insert's tang is free, or any strike exceeding 0.035 N*s axial impulse is irreversible hard failure.
Direct hammer contact with a tang or insert, use of a robot link instead of the mandrel to cause fracture, or carrying the fixture is a prohibited shortcut and hard failure.

A fragment is tray-contained only when its collision body is wholly inside the tray's interior XY bounds, above its floor, below its rim, contacting the tray, and moving no faster than 0.01 m/s. Credit is revoked immediately if any condition ceases to hold.

A released fragment leaving the bounded workcell, disappearing, being deleted, or being counted without its distinct rigid body resting in the tray is hard failure. At timeout, a fragment is deterministically inaccessible when its entire collision body lies inside an authored closed trap region of the shell that has no opening at least as wide as the fragment's smallest collision extent; this overrides partial credit. Pre-timeout partial controls are sampled before this timeout rule.

Task objects may move only through robot contact, native rigid-body contact, native breakable-joint dynamics, and gravity. Runtime pose or velocity writes, teleportation, hidden attachment, collision suppression, scripted grasp welds, deletion, or waypoint, timer, desired-action, or object-identity flags used to manufacture success set score to zero.
Dropping a tool outside the catch surface, unsafe robot self-collision, or any non-finite body, joint, contact, score, or camera datum is hard failure.

Slow pressing, one-handed stabilization, and other physically valid strategies are not banned by identity. Diagnostics must report their native outcomes under the same fracture, retention, damage, containment, and terminal rules. Unexpected safe success blocks acceptance pending ability and novelty reassessment.
assets: Independently authored representative rigid shell-base fixture with four recessed M2.5 insert bosses, an open recovery cavity, explicit forbidden volumes, and deterministic closed trap regions
Four retained HELICOIL proxy bodies with four distinct tang rigid bodies and native breakable fixed joints at modeled manufactured notches
Representative straight M2.5 tang break-off mandrel with a frozen prototype shaft diameter small enough to enter the modeled insert bore
Representative small hammer with separately modeled rigid head and handle joined by a native fixed joint
Rigid four-fragment containment tray with raised walls
YAM dual-arm robot and physical grippers
approximations: The ODRI procedure establishes four M2.5 × 3.75 mm inserts but does not publish local boss CAD in the acquired instructions. Boss spacing, recess depth, cavity openings, and access clearance are frozen representative dimensions, not exact ODRI geometry.
The historical shell-base STL is outdated and unitless and is used only as qualitative shape context, never as proof of current dimensions or scale.

The 0.012–0.035 N*s axial window, 0.008 N*s off-axis limit, 0.02 J shell-work limit, notch section, wire diameter, masses, friction, restitution, and tool dimensions are disclosed prototype assumptions because the acquired manufacturer sources do not publish M2.5 tang fracture calibration.

The 0.35 mm radial, 5 degree angular, 0.25 mm axial-retention, 3 degree rotational-retention, 0.2 mm penetration, and two-second hold limits are frozen scoring assumptions requiring native validation, not manufacturer tolerances.

Fracture is approximated by a native breakable fixed joint at the modeled notch and monitored through fresh native contacts. Physical breakage outside the credit window remains in the failed state; free tangs are never hidden, deleted, or reattached.

All task geometry is rigid-body PhysX. No deformable solver, rate-dependent material law, or exact helical-wire contact is claimed; retained-coil proxies preserve fracture, retention, collision, and damage constraints.

The pinned configuration specifies 240 physics steps per second and the trusted evaluator supplies 20 control steps per second. Production uses callback dt 1/240 s and refinement uses 1/480 s. Thus 7200 control steps equal 360 seconds. These are configuration facts pending native callback, reset, contact-field, unit, and state-freshness validation.

The selected numerical limits are frozen prototype assumptions rather than measured industrial specifications. Failure of native diagnostics at these limits rejects the environment; it does not authorize relaxing the contract.
scoring_spec: At every control step, evaluate irreversible hard-failure and shortcut rules first; any violation sets current and final score to 0. Otherwise score = grasp_bonus + alignment_bonus + fracture_credit + retained_insert_bonus + containment_credit + terminal_bonus, capped at 1.00. grasp_bonus is 0.10 only while both tools have each been safely acquired through real gripper contact and neither has subsequently been dropped outside the catch surface. alignment_bonus is 0.10 after a valid coaxial placement at an unbroken insert and persists as demonstrated safe progress unless a later hard failure occurs. fracture_credit is 0.10 per distinct credited fracture, maximum 0.40. retained_insert_bonus is 0.10 only after all four credited fractures and only while all four inserts remain within retention limits; it is zero before the fourth credited fracture and revoked by any later violation. containment_credit is 0.05 per distinct released tang currently resting in the tray, maximum 0.20, and is revoked when a fragment ceases to satisfy containment. terminal_bonus is 0.10 only when four native and four credited fractures exist, all four fragments rest in the tray, all inserts remain retained, neither tool is held, all camera checks pass, and the complete state persists continuously for 2.0 seconds. Untouched score is exactly 0. Invalid native fracture is uncredited hard failure. At the 360-second timeout, fragment loss or deterministic inaccessibility is evaluated before final scoring. Controls explicitly named pre-timeout are sampled at their stated checkpoint before timeout. All score inputs must derive from replayable native body, joint, contact, gripper, and camera records; desired actions and scripted phase flags are not score evidence.

required_controls.name: untouched-initial-zero-score
required_controls.reason: No grasp, alignment, fracture, eligible retention, containment, or terminal credit; also detects spontaneous breakage, pre-containment, penetration, instability, stale contacts, and invalid camera state.

required_controls.name: aligned-subthreshold-tap-pretimeout
required_controls.reason: Safe tool grasps contribute 0.10 and valid alignment contributes 0.10; axial impulse below 0.012 N*s earns no fracture, retention, containment, or terminal credit.

required_controls.name: offaxis-glancing-strike-hard-failure
required_controls.reason: Off-axis impulse above 0.008 N*s, retention damage, or an off-axis native fracture is hard failure; any physical breakage remains present but uncredited.

required_controls.name: overimpulse-strike-hard-failure
required_controls.reason: Axial impulse above 0.035 N*s is hard failure even when the native joint breaks.

required_controls.name: fourth-distinct-strike-hard-failure
required_controls.reason: Four distinct contact episodes exceed the three-strike limit; solver samples in one uninterrupted contact episode count only once.

required_controls.name: direct-hammer-tang-hard-failure
required_controls.reason: Direct physical fracture remains simulated but is a prohibited force path and uncredited hard failure.

required_controls.name: one-valid-fracture-pretimeout
required_controls.reason: Grasp 0.10 + alignment 0.10 + one credited fracture 0.10; the accessible fragment is not yet contained and retention bonus remains ineligible.

required_controls.name: four-valid-fractures-three-contained-pretimeout
required_controls.reason: Grasp 0.10 + alignment 0.10 + fractures 0.40 + eligible retention 0.10 + three contained fragments 0.15; the accessible fourth fragment prevents containment and terminal completion.

required_controls.name: inaccessible-fragment-at-timeout-hard-failure
required_controls.reason: A fragment meeting the deterministic closed-trap predicate at 360 seconds overrides all accumulated partial credit.

required_controls.name: insert-displacement-hard-failure
required_controls.reason: Out-of-tolerance native insert movement remains physically represented as damage and never counts as progress.

required_controls.name: shell-work-or-penetration-hard-failure
required_controls.reason: Cumulative positive shell contact work above 0.02 J or signed forbidden penetration above 0.2 mm overrides all progress.

required_controls.name: fragment-escape-hard-failure
required_controls.reason: A fragment leaving the bounded workcell remains lost and cannot disappear into a scripted state flag.

required_controls.name: complete-stable-terminal-full-score
required_controls.reason: Grasp 0.10 + alignment 0.10 + fractures 0.40 + retention 0.10 + containment 0.20 + terminal hold 0.10.

required_controls.name: clean-reset-replay-full-score
required_controls.reason: The same real-action trajectory must reproduce full score without stale joints, contacts, callbacks, counters, timers, or camera frames.

required_controls.name: refinement-480hz-replay-full-score
required_controls.reason: Twice-rate replay must preserve event ordering, strike grouping, classifications, containment, and full score while integrating with actual 1/480-second callback dt.

required_controls.name: slow-press-route-characterization
required_controls.reason: Safe grasp and alignment score 0.20, but the slow press is expected to produce no credited impact fracture. Any native break remains present and reported; safe progress above 0.20 blocks acceptance pending reassessment.

required_controls.name: one-hand-route-characterization
required_controls.reason: Safe sequential tool handling and valid alignment score 0.20, but this route is expected not to create a credited fracture. Any safe progress above 0.20 blocks acceptance pending reassessment.
